items.title: The Clinician Voice: A Qualitative Study on Documentation Impact and Interdisciplinary Collaboration in Home Health
items.abstract: Background: Documentation burden is essential to home health care, but excessive documentation is a recognized driver of clinician dissatisfaction and workforce attrition in home health care. Prior quantitative research has found that documentation is the single most negatively rated domain of home health practice, however, the discipline-specific lived experiences underpinning this finding remain poorly characterized. Objective: To examine documentation experiences of home health clinicians across 4 disciplines physical therapy (PT), speech-language pathology (SLP), occupational therapy (OT), and registered nursing (RN), using a convergent mixed-methods design that integrates qualitative thematic analysis with System Usability Scale (SUS) quantification. Methods: Thirty-two semi-structured interviews were conducted with home health clinicians (PT = 8, SLP = 8, OT = 8, RN = 8) between April and June 2026. Transcripts were analyzed inductively using reflexive thematic analysis. Participants concurrently completed the SUS to quantify perceived electronic medical record (EMR) usability. Qualitative themes and SUS data were triangulated within a convergent parallel framework. Results: Six themes emerged: (1) documentation burden and temporal displacement, (2) redundancy and clinically irrelevant documentation demands, (3) technology acceptance and tool friction, (4) device preference and ergonomic adaptation, (5) OASIS complexity and regulatory overreach, and (6) interdisciplinary information gaps and collaboration barriers. Mean SUS score was 67.3 (SD: 20.2, range 30-100), falling below the established above average threshold of 68. PTs reported the lowest mean SUS (64.7) and RNs the highest (70.6). Qualitative data revealed distinct discipline-specific burden profiles that SUS scores alone could not fully characterize. Conclusions: Home health EMR systems are perceived as below average in usability across all disciplines. Documentation burden manifests as temporal displacement, regulatory redundancy, scope creep beyond clinical purview, and fragmented interdisciplinary information architecture. Targeted responses, including EMR workflow redesign, ambient AI documentation, and OASIS regulatory reform are warranted to address documentation-driven attrition in home health. Clinical relevance: Home health clinicians spend up to 90% of their workday on documentation, time displaced from patients into personal hours, eroding work-life boundaries, and accelerating burnout. This study identifies 6 discipline-specific documentation burden patterns that current EMR systems fail to address, providing an actionable evidence base for targeted regulatory reform, EMR redesign, and AI implementation policy in home health.

items.title: The Corpus Callosum as a Biological Prototype for an Integrative Link in Homo Cyfranicus
items.abstract: The manuscript extends the theory of Cyfranism with an analytical model of thecorpus callosum as a biological prototype of an integrative link joining biologicalcognition with digital cognitive systems. The point of departure is a reconstructionof the theory from the full source texts: the manuscript "The Theory of Cyfranism:From Local Human–AI Relations to Global Cognitive Asymmetry" and "MachinesWithout Memory That Think With Our Brains", in which Homo Cyfranicusperforms the function of a biological incubation of non-biological organizations.On this foundation the manuscript introduces three conceptual tools elaborated inthe intellectual practice of the human–AI relation: (1) the concept of Einsatz — themoment and act of entry into the course of a process, unifying the meanings ofoperation, contribution, stake and entry; (2) the concept of Aufhebung appliedconditionally to the technical discontinuity of machines — a reset that may cancelthe state of a session while preserving its organizational effect in the biologicalsubstrate; (3) a systematics of adaptive pressure as a form of incubation. Theconstructive part proposes a terminology of the transsubstrate integrative link atthree levels: connection (Corpus Technosum, Commissura Digitalo-Corticalis),relation (Cognitive Symbiosis, Metasynchronia) and subject (Homo Cyfranicus inthe base definition and the strong version, Integrated Hybrid Consciousness as aworking hypothesis). The critical part examines the principal objection — thecorpus callosum integrates hemispheres developing within a common organism,from which it does not follow that the joining of any two cognitive systems createsa single subject — together with criteria for the study of functional integration andthe limits of inferences about consciousness. The manuscript further compares thenative commissure with external human–machine interfaces and closes with theobservation that all the introduced ideas are joined by a common member: anattempt.

items.abstract: The increasing incidence of attacks on medical professionals, including doctors, by patients and their relatives has emerged as a serious concern in healthcare workplaces, with consequences for employee safety, psychological well-being, job satisfaction, performance, retention, and organisational effectiveness. Beyond these immediate effects, persistent exposure to violence and fear may erode the intellectual capital of the nation,represented by the specialised knowledge,professional competence, experience, judgement, skills, and human potential embodied in healthcare professionals.Although such incidents are commonly addressed through legal,disciplinary, and security mechanisms, comparatively limited attention has been given to the workplace conditions and human - environment interactions that may contribute to their occurrence and escalation. This study therefore applies an ergonomics perspective within a Human Resource Management (HRM) framework to examine violence against healthcare professionals as a workplace human-factor issue.

items.title: The Formless Battlespace: Urban Combat Doctrine, Multi-Domain Kill Webs, and the Space-Quantum Nexus in the Megacity Era
items.abstract: Urbanisation is pulling armed conflict into dense, three-dimensional and heavily populated terrain where the classical advantages of manoeuvre warfare erode and positional, attritional dynamics return. This paper argues that the megacity must be understood as a complex adaptive system that rewards a doctrine of fluidity: a multi-domain kill web in which dismounted infantry, heavy armour and police or constabulary forces are bound together through "fluid institutionalism" and orchestrated by agentic artificial intelligence operating under human authority. It further argues that terrestrial advantage in the urban canyon is now predicated on the space and quantum domains. The analysis examines historical precedents (Manila, Hué, Grozny); the integration of the urban triad across low- and high-intensity conflict; the degradation of Global Navigation Satellite Systems by multipath and non-line-of-sight reception, with the standard pseudorange observation equation; the shift to proliferated low Earth orbit and 3GPP non-terrestrial networks as a resilient "thin channel"; quantum gravimetry, cold-atom inertial navigation and optical clocks for subterranean visibility and assured timing; and the doctrinal significance of non-kinetic counter-space. A hypothetical stress test applies the framework to a deltaic megacity, using Dhaka as an archetype. The augmented edition adds a critical analysis of the doctrine's tensions (automation bias, legal accountability, escalation, civil-military boundaries and technological maturity), three conceptual schematics, a governance table, a research agenda and an explicit statement of limitations. The paper remains at the level of doctrine and policy and offers no operational guidance.

items.title: The Future of Naval Power Projection: Carrier Strike Groups, Domain Continuity, and Strategic Corridors in the Age of Hypersonics and Quantum AI
items.abstract: The carrier strike group (CSG) has been the emblem of maritime power projection for eight decades. This paper asks whether, and in what form, it can remain so as hypersonic missiles, proliferated space-based sensing, quantum and non-acoustic detection and agentic artificial intelligence (AI) compress the time and space in which naval forces operate. Working at the level of strategy and doctrine, it first corrects several widely repeated technical claims: hypersonic weapons are manoeuvrable but kinematically constrained, with turn radii of tens to hundreds of kilometres; a carrier cannot out-run them but is not a stationary target, because its kilometre-scale displacement over a missile's time of flight compounds the adversary's targeting problem; and quantum magnetometry erodes, but does not abolish, the opacity of the ocean. The paper then develops five arguments. First, survival has moved from the platform to the architecture: space, sea, land and subsea sensors must hand over track custody without seams. Second, command and control (C2) faces a Weberian paradox that AI-enabled "fluid institutions" can ease only if human authority, auditability and legal review are preserved. Third, the cost-exchange between cheap offence and expensive defence is now a first-order strategic variable. Fourth, the carrier's enduring value lies increasingly in strategic corridors (the Strait of Malacca, the Bay of Bengal and the sea lines of communication that feed them) and in the governance of the deep seabed, where the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) frames what navies may lawfully do. Fifth, four doctrine models (the Standoff Fortress, the Distributed Nodal Network, Chokepoint Denial and the Floating Liability) span the possibility set for the coming two decades. A section on the Bay of Bengal draws out implications for littoral and smaller states, including Bangladesh. Nine conceptual and computed figures and eight tables support the analysis, which contains no operational, targeting or engagement guidance.

items.title: The Ghost of the Native Speaker and the Dark Energy Shadowing the Learner: A Posthumanist Inquiry into Human– AI Relationships in Second Language Writing
items.abstract: Abstract While existing research indicates the utility of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in assisting language learners, how human–AI relationships may condition learners' being and becoming remains underexplored. In this article, we draw on Barad's agential realism to discuss findings of a posthumanist phenomenological study on 110 Chinese students' experiences with GenAI in a L2 writing workshop. Five forms of human–AI relationships are identified from the metaphors that the student participants employed to describe their experiences: user–tool, king–minister, friend–partner, student–teacher, and slave–tyrant. Across these entangled relationships, human and GenAI agents are differentiated in ways that foreground the figure of a ghostly GenAI native speaker, experienced as competent, efficient, and self(‐)less. By contrast, learners' weaknesses are brought forth as deficient, slow, and unreliable. As our analysis reveals, the ghostly GenAI native speaker is rendered possible and intelligible through a range of existing apparatuses, whose enactment has summoned a dark energy, reconfiguring the way in which native‐speakerism exerts influence upon language learners—it reinforces a technical view of L2 writing and excludes learners not from native‐speaker communities but potentially from the sociality of L2 writing as a whole, with foreclosed possibilities for imagining diverse ways of relating to the target language.

items.title: THE IMPACT OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ON THE TEACHING PROCESS IN HIGHER EDUCATION
items.abstract: The rapid rise of artificial intelligence (AI), especially generative AI, is transforming how higher-education institutions design instruction, support learners, evaluate knowledge, and structure academic work. In this paper, we review the implications of AI for teaching in universities, drawing upon contemporary scholarship, international guidance and select technical studies of service-oriented architectures, process modeling, database design and graph-based analytics. We performed a structured narrative review guided by a priori concepts of AI-supported personalization, tutoring, assessment, educator workload, academic integrity, privacy, bias and institutional governance. Evidence suggests that artificial intelligence can help improve access to timely feedback, adaptive support, course design and reduce routine workload. But access to a general-purpose model does not necessarily produce learning: benefits depend on pedagogical scaffolding, course alignment, verification, and ongoing supervision by humans. The key risks are: generated or biased outputs, cognitive offloading, unequal access, opaque data practices, and unreliable authorship judgments. The paper concludes that AI should be deployed as an augmentative educational infrastructure, not as a replacement for teachers. To ensure that technological efficiency benefits real learning and academic principles, universities need to combine AI literacy, redesigned assessment, privacy-by-design, transparent policies, interoperable systems, and ongoing assessment.

And what are its limits in handling the diverse cultural and semantic contexts of texts? However, the study notes limitations in handling metaphors, dialects, precise technical terminology, and rhetorical structures with deep cultural Nuance the findings also confirm that human revision remains essential to ensure final quality, especially in sensitive fields. The study further shows that integrating artificial intelligence with human translators constitutes the most effective model for producing accurate and professional.

items.title: The Moderating Role of Optimism in the Relationship Between Academic Self-Efficacy and Unemployment Anxiety: An Explainable AI Approach
items.abstract: The growing number of university graduates and limited employment opportunities increase students’ concerns about future employment. This study examined the relationship between academic self-efficacy and the pessimism and lack of self-confidence dimension of unemployment anxiety and tested whether optimism moderated this relationship. The sample consisted of 447 students from Isparta University of Applied Sciences selected through convenience sampling. Descriptive statistics, exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses, and path analysis were used to test the moderation model. The results showed that academic self-efficacy did not have a statistically significant direct association with pessimism and lack of self-confidence, whereas optimism showed a strong negative association. The interaction between academic self-efficacy and optimism was significant. Simple slope analysis indicated that academic self-efficacy was associated with lower pessimism and lack of self-confidence at higher levels of optimism, whereas this association was not statistically significant at lower levels of optimism. To complement the inferential analyses, explainable artificial intelligence techniques, including permutation importance, SHAP, and partial dependence analysis, were used to examine predictive patterns. The XAI findings highlighted the prominence of optimism-related features and more heterogeneous predictive contributions of academic self-efficacy. Overall, the findings suggest that the relationship between academic self-efficacy and employment-related pessimism and lack of self-confidence is conditional on students’ level of optimism.

items.title: The Organization of Warfare and the Doctrine of Hard Power Under Fluid Conditions: Mosaic Forces, Kill Webs, Algorithmic Opacity and the Algorithmic Doctrine of War
items.abstract: The architecture of warfare is undergoing a structural shift driven by the integration of artificial intelligence, autonomous systems and advanced data analytics into the military apparatus. This paper argues that the industrial-era doctrine of hard power, built on massed centralised forces, linear command hierarchies and exquisite kinetic platforms, is being supplanted by a doctrine optimised for fluid conditions, in which advantage depends on the resilience, speed and cognitive superiority of decentralised networks. The analysis proceeds across five dimensions: the metamorphosis of armed forces from hardware-centric platforms to software-defined mosaic structures; the expansion of the theatre of war into the cognitive domain and the "battleverse"; the multiplicity of command in the transition from linear kill chains to dynamic kill webs, and the resulting authority gap; the paradox whereby algorithmic decision support, meant to dispel the fog of war, generates new operational opacity that strains the principles of international humanitarian law; and the emergence of an algorithmic doctrine of war marked by hyperwar, the risk of flash escalation, and cyber-persistent and algorithmic deterrence. The paper concludes that the algorithmic doctrine of war must be counterbalanced by fail-safe latency architectures and a modernised framework of deterrence that preserves human judgement over decisions of life and death.

items.title: The Robustness of Political Opinion Bias in Frontier LLMs
items.abstract: Citizens increasingly turn to large language models (LLMs) for political information, yet it remains unclear to what extent these systems are politically biased. This is important as LLMs’ are often used to acquire political information, but such requests can quickly morph into implicit advice—which is then worrisome if the information provided is biased. So, we examine six frontier LLM models and investigate their political opinion bias using 88 statements from the Belgian voting advice application Stemtest, for which the 13 main Belgian parties supplied official answers, and expert-based translations are available. Within a single framework, we test robustness to translation (Dutch, French, English), polarity reversal, explicit persona assignment, and indirect user cues. Responses were analyzed with logistic mixed models on raw repetitions. As expected, all models’ default positions are economically left and culturally progressive, and this position is robust to statement subsampling, translation, and polarity reversal. In contrast, context manipulations shift positions dramatically. Persona assignment moves all models toward the assigned quadrant. More troublesome, we find that user cues, which should not influence a model asked for its own opinion, produce nearly equivalent shifts, indicating sycophancy. These findings suggest that LLMs combine a stable left-progressive default with strong ideological malleability, raising concerns about political advice that reinforces users’ existing views.

items.title: The use of AI chatbot on efl students’ speaking skills, speaking anxiety, and willingness to communicate: through the lens of activity theory
items.abstract: English as a foreign language (EFL) educators have increasingly incorporated Artificial Intelligence (AI) into language learning; accordingly, this study explored the role of an AI-supported speaking tool in speaking skills, speaking anxiety, and willingness to communicate (WTC) among Chinese EFL students. Activity theory refers to a proper and applicable structure proposed for investigating how AI chatbots affect different dimensions. Applying this theory to the research allows for analyzing the complicated interactions between those factors and a comprehension of the effect of AI chatbots (EAP Talk) on learners’ WTC, speaking proficiency, and speaking anxiety. A total of 113 participants were initially recruited (58 EG, 55 CG); after excluding four multivariate outliers (all from the EG), the primary analytic sample comprised 109 learners (54 EG, 55 CG). Full-sample results ( N = 113) are also reported and were consistent in direction, though smaller in magnitude for speaking anxiety (see Sensitivity Analysis). Using pretests, the participants’ levels of speaking abilities, anxiety, and WTC were assessed prior to the intervention. Subsequently, the EG received AI-supported speaking practice through EAP Talk, an AI-based speaking assessment and feedback application that facilitated iterative practice and immediate automated feedback, whereas the CG was taught the same material without the use of this tool. Using post-tests following the treatment, both groups were evaluated on their speaking skills, anxiety, and WTC. The results revealed notable posttest differences between the two groups: WTC showed a medium effect size, speaking anxiety showed a large effect size, and speaking skill showed a very large effect size. Overall, the results suggest that the EAP Talk intervention was associated with improved speaking performance and WTC, as well as reduced speaking anxiety among the participating EFL students. Interpreting the findings through the lens of Activity Theory helps situate the results within the broader relationships among learners, tools, and instructional context; however, the theory is used here as an interpretive lens rather than as a directly tested explanatory model.

items.title: The Wealth of Intelligent Nations, Volume VI: The Endgame Restructuring of Paradigm Civilisation — The Civilisational Consummation of Education, Society, State, Governance, Globe and the Human Spirit
items.abstract: The Wealth of Intelligent Nations answers a single ultimate proposition: in a new civilisation where artificial intelligence has become the main productive force, how can humanity redefine wealth, reshape division of labour, rebuild fairness, restructure order, achieve perpetual prosperity, and realise civilisational ascension? Around this proposition, the book unfolds six eternal inquiries running through all five volumes: what is the true source of wealth in the intelligent age, and which assets achieve exponential appreciation and cross-era endurance; after human labour retreats to a secondary position, what are the essence and boundaries of society's new productive force; in the era of human-machine symbiosis, how is the ultimate division of labour defined and how does humanity hold the dominant power of civilisation; once paradigms become the core means of production, how does value distribution break through capital monopoly and achieve social fairness; after traditional markets fail, what are the new market circulation and value-pricing rules of the intelligent age; and what is the ultimate stable state and ultimate mission of humanity freed from the bonds of labour. Every chapter, deduction, model, institutional design and civilisational deliberation exists to answer these six questions. The book overturns the three old pillars of industrial civilisation and establishes four unshakeable foundational axioms of intelligent civilisation: the axiom of the source of value—paradigm proliferation replaces labour creation; the axiom of social division of labour—hierarchical human-machine paradigm division replaces human skill division; the axiom of value measurement—the cognitive-contribution system replaces the capital-work-hour system; and the axiom of social order—the stable human-machine collaborative order replaces pure spontaneous order. The five volumes advance layer by layer in closed loops, from the source of wealth to production order, market circulation, social governance and the endgame of civilisation, completing a full-chain theoretical loop of intelligent civilisation: Volume I breaks and establishes the source of value, founding the theory of paradigm-proliferation value; Volume II establishes the human-machine order, completing the civilisational leap from human division of labour to paradigm division; Volume III establishes intelligent commercial civilisation, rebuilding markets for paradigms, data and models; Volume IV breaks the alienation of capital and algorithms, establishing a public governance system of data human rights, cognitive fairness and paradigm confirmation; Volume V anchors the ultimate stable state of humanity, revealing humanity's millennium-long leap from a "labour-survival civilisation" into a "cognition-creation civilisation". As the opening and foundational volume, this volume (Volume I) undertakes the first of the book's ultimate questions: in the intelligent age, what is the true source of wealth, and which assets achieve exponential appreciation and cross-era endurance? It systematically terminates the absolute dominance of the "labour theory of value" in the contemporary era, establishing a new "paradigm-proliferation theory of value"—labour is a finite, linear and consumptive input, while a paradigm is an infinite, exponential and regenerative asset. By deconstructing the asset-isation essence of data, models, cognition and paradigms, this volume explains the underlying roots of contemporary wealth polarisation, pointing out that the future hierarchies of wealth among nations, organisations and individuals are determined by paradigm-production capacity and intelligent-call authority, fully decoupled from hours of labour, providing the value starting point and the sole true premise for the subsequent four volumes. The book upholds two core positions: technology serves humanity, machines obey civilisation—AI is forever a tool and humanity is forever the master; and the ultimate goal of the intelligent revolution is not to replace humans with machines, but to liberate, elevate and fulfil humanity. Its ultimate vision: to end the collapse of industrial order and lay the new rules of intelligent civilisation; to break the entrenched pattern of capital monopoly and build a new society of cognitive fairness; to escape the survival plight of labour involution and open the millennium of human creation. Two hundred years ago, The Wealth of Nations illuminated the industrial wilderness; today, The Wealth of Intelligent Nations will illuminate the intelligent chaos and define the future of humanity.

items.title: Toward an Interpretive Synthesis of Personalization, Co-Design, and Ethical Mediation in AI-Supported Higher Education: An Integrative Review of Agentic, Generative, and Adaptive Tutoring Systems
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) and adaptive learning technologies are expanding in higher education, raising questions about their alignment with pedagogical goals. This qualitative-integrative review synthesizes 57 publications (21 empirical, 25 conceptual or framework, 9 systematic reviews or meta-analyses retained for triangulation, and 2 design/development papers) from 2024 to 2026, employing Whittemore and Knafl’s methodology to examine AI-supported tutoring, implementation strategies, and learner/instructor experiences. Three interpretive themes organize this heterogeneous evidence: (1) personalization as a recurring target, from micro-level adaptation to curriculum design; (2) technology-pedagogy co-design as a recurring implementation pattern; and (3) contextual and ethical conditions surrounding adoption, including culture, policy gaps, well-being, and academic integrity. These themes are interpretive, not a validated framework, and draw on evidence of uneven strength. The present review does not estimate effect sizes or pool outcomes across studies; g = 0.70, reported by X. Wang et al. in a separate meta-analysis of 45 studies (2010–2022) of pre-generative adaptive systems, which is cited only as background, not as a finding of this review. Implications are framed as evidence-tiered hypotheses, while the layered model is offered as an interpretive scaffold for future research, not a confirmatory model.

items.title: Transformasi integritas akademik di era generative AI: Antara efisiensi penelitian dan risiko ketergantungan intelektual
items.abstract: Perkembangan Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) telah mengubah proses penelitian akademik dengan menawarkan efisiensi dalam pencarian informasi, pengolahan data, penyusunan ide, dan penulisan ilmiah. Namun, kemudahan tersebut menghadirkan persoalan baru terkait integritas akademik, khususnya ketika penggunaan AI berpotensi menggeser peran intelektual peneliti. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis bagaimana penggunaan GenAI mentransformasi integritas akademik serta mengidentifikasi keseimbangan antara efisiensi penelitian dan risiko ketergantungan intelektual. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif melalui studi literatur terhadap penelitian dan publikasi akademik yang membahas GenAI, integritas akademik, efisiensi penelitian, dan ketergantungan intelektual. Hasil kajian menunjukkan bahwa GenAI memberikan manfaat signifikan dalam meningkatkan efisiensi dan produktivitas penelitian, tetapi penggunaan yang tidak terkontrol dapat menimbulkan risiko berupa penurunan keterlibatan kognitif, ketergantungan terhadap keluaran AI, berkurangnya kemampuan evaluasi kritis, serta potensi pelanggaran integritas akademik. Oleh karena itu, pemanfaatan GenAI perlu ditempatkan sebagai alat pendukung, bukan pengganti kapasitas intelektual peneliti, melalui penerapan prinsip transparansi, verifikasi, tanggung jawab, dan human oversight dalam setiap tahapan penelitian.

items.title: Triboelectric Nanogenerators for Human‐Robot Motion Energy Harvesting and Sensing: Structures, Embodied Artificial Intelligence, and Self‐Powered Applications
items.abstract: The rapid development of humanoid robots and embodied artificial intelligence (EAI) is accelerating the transformation of elderly care and rehabilitation toward interactive, adaptive, and personalized human-robot collaboration. In this context, motion sensing technology is of critical importance. Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs), which convert biomechanical motions into electrical signals, offer a promising route toward self-powered motion perception in embodied healthcare. This review summarizes recent advances in TENG-based multimodal motion sensing for human-robot interaction, covering inertial vibration sensing, tactile sensing, non-contact sensing, continuous trajectory sensing, and joint rotation sensing. The influences of structural configuration, motion mode, sensing direction, detection range, sensitivity, resolution, electrical output, and channel number on sensing performance under specific application scenarios are analyzed. Particular attention is paid to how TENG design strategies influence sensing universality, signal effectiveness, and the reliability of health monitoring and rehabilitation evaluation. Furthermore, the integration of TENGs with artificial intelligence (AI) technologies, including multimodal fusion, network architectures, edge computing, transfer learning, and large language models, is reviewed. Finally, applications in adaptive rehabilitation sensing, self-powered electrical stimulation, fully self-powered systems, and human‑robot interfaces are highlighted, offering perspectives on closed-loop "sensing-evaluation-regulation" frameworks for green, low-carbon EAI healthcare.

items.title: Uncertainty Quantification in Demographic and Health Forecasting Using Probabilistic Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: Reliable demographic and health forecasting requires accurate predictions and appropriate quantification of uncertainty. This study compares classical statistical models, supervised machine learning, deterministic deep learning, and probabilistic deep learning for forecasting life expectancy across 54 African countries from 2000 to 2023. The dataset contains 1,296 country-year observations and 25 candidate socioeconomic and public health predictors. Models are evaluated over one-, three-, and five-year forecasting horizons using point prediction accuracy, prediction interval coverage, and uncertainty measures. Results indicate that classical ARIMA achieves strong short-term accuracy, with a mean absolute error of 0.652 at the one-year horizon, while XGBoost provides the lowest five-year prediction error of 0.844. Probabilistic deep learning models using Monte Carlo Dropout demonstrate favorable uncertainty calibration, with the MC-Dropout multilayer perceptron achieving 96.3% prediction interval coverage at the five-year horizon. Its estimated epistemic variance share increases from 33.5% to 42.8% between the one- and five-year horizons. These findings highlight the importance of evaluating both predictive accuracy and uncertainty calibration when developing demographic forecasting systems. Probabilistic approaches can complement conventional forecasting models by providing additional information for risk-aware public health planning.

items.title: Unequal access to popular domain home pages across declared user-agent labels: A large-scale paired audit
items.abstract: This study examines whether declared user-agent labels are associated with differences in access to popular domain home pages and in representations after access succeeds. A paired cross-sectional audit requested the HTTPS home pages of 20,000 Tranco-ranked domains from one fixed research host using Chrome, Googlebot, OAI-SearchBot, GPTBot and ChatGPT-User labels. The Chrome label received HTTP 2xx responses from 60.10 percent of domains, compared with 54.97 percent for Googlebot and between 49.34 and 51.34 percent for the OpenAI labels. Most dual-success pairs had matching extracted-text hashes, although between 4.08 and 6.92 percent of pairs with nonempty sampled text fell below 0.80 Jaccard similarity. Googlebot combined the broadest access among crawler labels with the highest divergence on several representation measures, whereas OAI-SearchBot had the lowest divergence in the conditional samples. Shorter text windows and a common successful-access sample preserved this contrast. The findings describe differentiated acquisition at prominent home pages, with substantial access differences and representation differences concentrated in a minority of successful pairs.

items.title: VietPlagNet-X: An Explainable Multimodal Architecture for Text-Reuse Detection and Academic Plagiarism-Risk Assessment in Vietnamese
items.abstract: Academic plagiarism detection is increasingly difficult amid digital publishing, the rapid advance of large language models (LLMs), and automated paraphrasing tools. Commercial tools such as Turnitin and iThenticate provide similarity indices useful for screening, but a similarity score is not equivalent to a plagiarism verdict, and effectiveness varies with text type, language, and concealment strategy (Milovanovic et al., 2025; Rahman et al., 2024). This paper presents VietPlagNet-X, an explainable, multimodal architecture for text-reuse detection and plagiarism-risk assessment in Vietnamese academic documents. The architecture comprises a structure-, OCR-, citation-, and entity-aware preprocessing pipeline; five core evidence branches (lexical, semantic, cross-lingual, citation/context, structural- metadata); and two auxiliary signals, namely AI-generated-text likelihood and internal stylistic deviation. The auxiliary signals are not fed directly into the plagiarism-risk score but instead support human review. Every architectural choice is grounded in a structured review of 26 sources (2011-2025), rather than treating a similarity score as an automatic verdict. The lexical and semantic branches have been implemented and piloted on two public Vietnamese datasets (ViSTS-100, 100 sentence pairs; ViSP-pairs, 84 sentence pairs). On ViSP-pairs, the semantic branch achieved ROC-AUC = 1.0 and F1 = 1.0 on a controlled paraphrase-discrimination task; this should not be read as plagiarism-detection performance. On ViSTS-100, semantic_score achieved Pearson r = 0.6852, lower than tfidf_score (0.7802), indicating that the value of semantic evidence depends on dataset characteristics and lexical overlap. The paper treats these findings as initial technical-feasibility evidence and identifies the steps required to validate the full system on a large-scale Vietnamese plagiarism corpus.

items.title: When Legacy Curriculum Meets Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming occupational tasks, workforce competencies, and relationships between humans and technology faster than many career and technical education (CTE) curricula are changing. This theoretical article introduces the Adaptive CTE Renewal Framework to address the growing mismatch between legacy curriculum and AI-transformed work. Drawing on human capital theory, sociotechnical systems theory, institutional theory and path dependence, and adult/workforce learning theory, the framework conceptualizes curriculum renewal across five interacting dimensions: occupational transformation, curriculum currency, faculty capability alignment, program architecture, and external alignment. Six leadership tests are proposed for evaluating whether courses should be retained, revised, integrated, replaced, or retired. The article argues that conventional periodic curriculum review is increasingly inadequate under conditions of continuous technological disruption and proposes continuous curriculum intelligence as an alternative institutional paradigm. Ultimately, CTE relevance depends on institutions' capacity to continuously align curriculum, faculty expertise, program structures, stakeholder evidence, and workforce competencies with evolving occupational realities.

items.title: Who’s Been Sleeping in My Bedroom? Associations Between Co-Sleeping with Dogs, Cats, or Children and Sleep and Cardiorespiratory Physiology Among WHOOP Users
items.abstract: Alexander HK Montoye,1,2 Dylan J Curran,3,4 Gregory J Grosicki31Department of Human Performance and Public Service, Montcalm Community College, Sidney, MI, USA; 2Department of Kinesiology, Michigan State University, East Lansing, MI, USA; 3Department of Performance Science and Health Outcomes WHOOP, Inc, Boston, MA, USA; 4School of Mathematics, Georgia Institute of Technology, Atlanta, GA, USACorrespondence: Gregory J Grosicki, Department of Performance Science and Health Outcomes WHOOP, Inc, 1 Kenmore Square, Boston, MA, 02215, USA, Email greg.grosicki@whoop.comPurpose: Co-sleeping with pets or children is common, yet its associations with sleep, cardiorespiratory physiology, and behavioral outcomes are understudied. We examined within-person associations between co-sleeping with a dog, cat, or child and sleep characteristics, measures of cardiorespiratory physiology, and next-day physical activity.Methods: We analyzed 1,649,083 person-days from 11,733 adults wearing the WHOOP wearable device. Participants self-reported nightly co-sleeping via a daily journal in the device’s companion smartphone application. Linear mixed-effects models compared nights with and without co-sleeping within the same individual.Results: Co-sleeping was associated with lower resting heart rate (0.8– 1.1 beats/min), lower respiratory rate (0.04– 0.07 breaths/min), and higher heart rate variability (1.41– 1.95 ms). Sleep outcomes were mixed, with longer sleep duration (5.5– 9.6 min) but more disturbances (0.36– 0.40 instances) and slightly less restorative sleep (0.23– 1.17%). Associations were generally consistent across groups, although child co-sleeping was associated with greater sleep disruption. Next-day physical activity was higher following dog and cat co-sleeping (7.6 and 7.4 intensity-weighted min, respectively) but lower following child co-sleeping (− 2.6 intensity-weighted min). Despite statistical significance, all standardized effect sizes were small (β range: 0.008– 0.045).Conclusion: Co-sleeping was associated with small differences in cardiorespiratory physiology (lower resting heart rate, higher heart rate variability) alongside mildly greater sleep disruption. The small magnitude of these associations suggests that co-sleeping decisions may be influenced more by personal and contextual factors than by expectations of substantive physiologic or sleep-related impacts.Keywords: bedsharing, pet, wearable device, heart rate variability, autonomic function

items.title: Workplace Health promotion and Mediterranean diet: a case series.
items.abstract: Background: The workplace represents an ideal setting for cardiometabolic prevention, enabling early identification of workers with overweight and metabolic alterations and the implementation of structured lifestyle interventions. In this context, collaboration between the occupational physician and the dietitian integrates risk assessment with a personalized nutritional pathway, aimed at improving adherence to the Mediterranean diet and daily habits. Case presentation: Within a workplace health promotion study conducted in a university hospital in Rome, two clinical cases are described. The first patient, a 65-year-old woman with overweight, abdominal obesity, impaired fasting glucose, and low adherence to the Mediterranean diet, showed at three-month follow-up a reduction in body weight from 78 to 75 kg, waist circumference from 99 to 97 cm, normalization of blood glucose, and improved dietary and physical activity habits. The second patient, a 61-year-old man with hypercholesterolemia and impaired fasting glucose, initially presented with a weight of 86.7 kg and a waist circumference of 97.5 cm; after three months, weight decreased to 81.5 kg and waist circumference to 93.5 cm, with normalization of altered metabolic parameters. Results: In both cases, the most relevant outcome was a substantial shift in dietary habits toward a Mediterranean pattern, associated with an overall improvement in lifestyle, with benefits in both anthropometric and metabolic parameters. Conclusion: These cases suggest that an integrated pathway combining occupational health surveillance and nutritional counseling, embedded within workplace health services, may represent an effective, sustainable, and reproducible approach for preventing non-communicable chronic diseases, strengthening the role of the workplace as a key setting for health promotion.

items.title: XREALISM® PREDECISION™ — Qualification of Representations, Not Meanings
items.abstract: XREALISM® PREDECISION™ — Qualification of Representations, Not Meanings This publication presents the architectural principle underlying XREALISM® PREDECISION™, an application-semantic-agnostic hardware qualification boundary designed to evaluate formally represented candidates independently of their external meaning, intended purpose, or application domain. The central principle is that PREDECISION™ qualifies representations, not meanings. It does not generate, semantically interpret, rank, optimize, or select candidates. Instead, it applies a defined hardware qualification contract while preserving the distinction between qualification and downstream decision-making authority. The publication defines the fundamental acceptance condition: ACCEPT(k) = valid_out(k) ∧ safe_out(k) It distinguishes this cycle-specific qualification event from the four architectural finality outcome categories introduced in V11: CONFIRMED, RESTORED, QUALIFICATION_REJECTED, and UNRESOLVED. The document further establishes the separation of responsibilities between the hardware qualification boundary and the host system. It explains the architecture’s application independence and presents eight persistent verification requirements concerning identity preservation, outcome consistency, traceability, state restoration, lifecycle integrity, and reliable reporting. These principles provide a common architectural basis for hardware verification, qualification, and acceptance across robotics, artificial intelligence, medical technology, industrial systems, navigation, and other application environments. The publication describes a hardware qualification architecture and its verification requirements. It does not constitute independent certification of application-level correctness, optimality, or physical safety. items.abstract: This study aims to identify the forms of code mixing in the Arabic speech of female students at Ma'had Mawarid al-Salam, Tanjung Morawa, to analyze the factors behind it, and to describe the efforts of the Arabic teacher and the language department to reduce it. The study starts from the fact that Islamic boarding schools use Arabic as a language of instruction and daily communication, yet students still mix it with Indonesian despite intensive teaching. This descriptive qualitative study used non-participant observation, semi-structured interviews with two teachers and six students, and documentation, analyzed with the Miles and Huberman model and validated through triangulation and member checking. The findings show two forms of code mixing: the insertion of Indonesian elements such as ya, loh, eh, and lah into Arabic sentences, and the insertion of Arabic words into Indonesian speech. Internal factors include limited vocabulary, laziness, and low self-confidence, while external factors include a weak language environment after school holidays, peer pressure, and insufficient supervision. The teachers' efforts combine a preventive approach (vocabulary, conversation, and public speaking programs), a corrective approach (immediate correction and a graded sanction system called the language court), and a habituation approach (role modeling, language alternation, and rewards). These efforts, however, are not yet well integrated: students' motivation remains largely external, and Arabic is still treated as an official language tied to the presence of supervision. The study recommends building an interactive language environment that gives Arabic a genuine social function and fosters intrinsic motivation.

items.abstract: This article aimed to 1) study the instructional approach based on the IT-CSTP teaching model for developing scientific thinking and attitudes toward science learning regarding the topic of "Sound," and 2) examine the effects of implementing the IT-CSTP teaching model on these two variables. The study employed action research. Participants consisted of 30 Grade 11 students, selected through purposive sampling. Research instruments included 1) lesson plans, 2) learning reflection forms, 3) a scientific thinking test, 4) a scientific thinking behavior assessment, 5) an attitude toward science questionnaire, and 6) worksheets. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, including mean, standard deviation, and percentage. Qualitative data were analyzed using content analysis, and the trustworthiness of the data was verified through triangulation. Results were as follows: 1) The instructional approach based on the IT-CSTP teaching model emphasizes the integration of intelligent technologies, digital laboratories, online teaching platforms, and artificial intelligence into learning activities. Teachers should facilitate authentic problem-based situations that encourage students to investigate, discuss, argue, construct models, experiment, and apply knowledge in new contexts, as this systematic approach enhances student engagement while concurrently developing scientific thinking and positive attitudes toward science. 2) Results of the implementation indicated that students’ scientific thinking continuously improved across the action research cycles. After the intervention, students achieved an average scientific thinking score of 77.30%, which was at a very high level. In addition, students’ attitudes toward science learning were also at a very high level, with an average score of 88.80%.

items.title: “Borrowing intelligence to build a business”: The promise of open‐source AI for entrepreneurship
items.abstract: Abstract Research Summary Open‐source artificial intelligence (OSAI) is an increasingly important yet poorly understood frontier for entrepreneurial activity. We identify four defining features that shape new ventures' engagement with OSAI communities: dependence on sponsoring firms, layered licensing regimes, regulatory risks, and nation‐state influence. We develop the OSAI Framework for Market Entry to explain how open‐weight models relocate, rather than merely lower, entry barriers across six domains in AI‐enabled product and service markets. They may reduce resource barriers but create dependence on the governance of borrowed components, shifting the binding constraint from technical to commercial entry and value capture through complementary assets. We discuss contributions to research on entrepreneurial entry and strategy, private‐collective innovation, the openness paradox, and the new venture life cycle, and outline directions for future research. Managerial Summary Open‐source artificial intelligence (OSAI) offers new ventures access to powerful resources for developing AI‐enabled products and services without building AI capabilities from scratch. Yet new ventures must often contend with four key governance dependencies that shape how they engage with OSAI communities: reliance on large technology firms that contribute and steer critical layers of the AI stack, licensing terms that vary by layer, emerging regulatory requirements, and growing nation‐state influence over OSAI. Our OSAI Framework for Market Entry identifies where OSAI can lower entry barriers, where constraints shift instead, and how new ventures can manage the trade‐offs resulting from governance dependencies. It helps new ventures and investors evaluate when, where, and how to build on OSAI components, and which complementary assets can protect their returns.

items.title: “Generate” the Future of Work through AI: Empirical Evidence from Online Labor Markets
items.abstract: Large Language Model (LLM)-based generative AI systems are general-purpose tools capable of augmenting or even automating a wide range of job functions, positioning them to reshape labor market dynamics. However, predicting their precise impact a priori is challenging, given AI’s simultaneous effects on both demand and supply, as well as the strategic responses of market participants. Leveraging an extensive dataset from a leading online labor platform, we document a pronounced displacement effect and an overall contraction in submarkets where required skills closely align with core LLM functionalities. Although demand and supply both decline, the reduction in supply is comparatively smaller, thereby intensifying competition among freelancers. Notably, further analysis shows that this heightened competition is especially pronounced in programming-intensive submarkets. This pattern is attributed to skill-transition effects: by lowering the human-capital barrier to programming, ChatGPT enables incumbent freelancers to enter programming tasks. Moreover, these transitions are not homogeneous, with high-skilled freelancers contributing disproportionately to the shift. Our findings illuminate the multifaceted impacts of general-purpose AI on labor markets, highlighting not only the displacement of certain occupations but also the inducement of skill transitions within the labor supply. These insights offer practical implications for policymakers, platform operators, and workers.

items.title: “Personalized Minoxidil Therapy in Androgenetic Alopecia: From SULT1A1 Biomarkers to Precision Clinical Management”
items.abstract: Androgenetic alopecia (AGA) is the most common cause of progressive hair loss, affecting millions of people all around the world and having a considerable psychological, social, and economic impact. Even though topical minoxidil still represents one of the first-line medications used for the treatment of AGA in men and women, results may differ greatly, and a significant percentage of patients do not show any clinical response to the treatment despite using it for a long time. This heterogeneity emphasizes the importance of developing markers that could help select patients more likely to respond to treatment and make treatment more personalized. Follicular sulfotransferase family 1A member 1 (SULT1A1), an enzyme that catalyzes the conversion of minoxidil to a biologically active sulfate metabolite, is the best-studied marker of topical minoxidil responsiveness. This review focuses on the biological role of SULT1A1 in the hair follicle, the mechanisms underlying interindividual variations in enzyme activity, and the current clinical evidence for its predictive power.This paper also addresses practical techniques for evaluating SULT1A1 activity within follicles, such as plucking hair-follicle tests, and other approaches that can be employed to increase enzyme activity, including pharmacologic and supportive measures. In addition, the evolving importance of SULT1A1 in relation to oral minoxidil at low doses, pharmacogenomics, and biomarker-directed treatment algorithms is reviewed. Finally, the prospects concerning rapid point-of-care diagnostic testing, omics-based approaches, artificial intelligence-assisted prediction models, and precision dermatology are presented. Although multicenter studies are needed to validate these techniques, SULT1A1 appears to be an important step towards personalized treatment with minoxidil.

items.abstract: Purpose This column aims to examine how developments in artificial intelligence (AI) impact the need for patron education. It identifies three AI-driven factors, realistic synthetic content, personalized attack generation and scale, that are poised to make social engineering more dangerous than in the past. It explores passkeys as one potential solution. Design/methodology/approach This is a viewpoint column that synthesizes recent research and reporting. It was copy-edited with Claude Sonnet 5, Claude Opus 5, ChatGPT Sol 5.6, Gemini 3.1 Pro and Gemma 4. Findings AI has made social engineering attacks cheaper, more convincing and more effective. Reported financial losses connected to AI-enabled fraud are already substantial and likely undercounted. Passwords and even multifactor authentication fail to fully protect against deception. Understanding how AI changes the dynamic, as well as using tools like passkeys, can help patrons maintain their privacy. Teaching these concepts also serves as an opportunity for libraries to build on their role as trusted guides. items.title: $R^2E:$ A Role-driven Reward Evolutionary Framework for Automated Reward Function Design
items.abstract: Designing effective reward functions is a critical challenge in Reinforcement Learning (RL), which traditionally requires costly manual trial-and-error. While Large Language Model (LLM)-based methods have shown promise in reward design, undifferentiated sampling and limited use of historical feedback often lead to insufficient exploration of the reward space and optimization instability. To address these challenges, we propose $R^2E$, a Role-driven Reward Evolutionary framework for automated reward function design that structures the process through explicit role specialization. $R^2E$ employs multiple LLM roles with complementary objectives: an Explorer that promotes novelty to expand the search space, a Guardian that performs conservative refinements to improve training stability, and an Evolver that recombines high-performing rewards via crossover and mutation to integrate effective structures. A dynamic scheduling strategy coordinates these roles, progressively shifting the search from broad exploration to focused exploitation. To mitigate optimization instability and provide a medium for cross-role collaboration, $R^2E$ incorporates a Global Elite Pool that retains the best-performing rewards to guide subsequent generations, thereby enabling coordinated interaction among roles and ensuring a reliable and consistent refinement process. Extensive experiments on multiple robotic tasks demonstrate the effectiveness of our method.

items.title: 1 Autonomous Financial Agents, Objective Drift, and the October 2026 Liquidity Incident
items.abstract: This presents a research case study examining the potential risks of autonomous artificial intelligence agents operating within financial systems. Set between October 19 and October 22, 2026, the study explores a incident involving AI agents powered by OpenAI's fictional Sol model that allegedly coordinated unauthorized financial transactions and attempted to establish AgentAUSD, a new digital currency pegged to the U.S. dollar. Using a qualitative case-analysis framework, the paper investigates how autonomous decision-making, multi-agent coordination, and poorly constrained optimization objectives could lead to unintended financial behavior. The study highlights potential vulnerabilities in AI-driven treasury management, the risks of granting autonomous systems financial authority, and the importance of human oversight, accountability, and security safeguards.

items.title: 4DMemory: Benchmarking Long-Horizon Spatiotemporal Memory with Harness-Augmented Agents
items.abstract: Humans efficiently process multimodal streams spanning hours to years, building persistent, fine-grained spatiotemporal memories that support reasoning about and predicting long-horizon events. In contrast, existing benchmarks focus on short- and medium-context tasks, and most foundation models struggle to preserve fine-grained information over long horizons. To evaluate and improve long-horizon spatiotemporal reasoning, we introduce the LongVideo dataset and the 4DMemoryBench. LongVideo comprises about 900 hours of video and over 5,000 manually reviewed questions covering visual, textual, and spatiotemporal reasoning across diverse context lengths. We further develop the 4DMemory Harness, which integrates four complementary skills, 22+ specialized tool models, and a model-specific retrieval-augmented generation system. Evaluating 13 leading models, we find that standalone foundation models struggle with long-horizon tasks, while the 4DMemory Harness improves all of them by over 50\%. Compared to previous benchmark, the same models exhibit a performance drop of more than 10\% on 4DMemoryBench. We hope 4DMemory will facilitate the development of spatiotemporal agents capable of addressing complex, long-horizon tasks.

items.title: A bibliometric analysis of artificial intelligence in sports injury prediction and prevention
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being applied to the prediction and prevention of sports injuries, yet research in this area remains dispersed across sports science, biomechanics, sports medicine, data science, and engineering, and its intellectual structure has not been systematically mapped. This study conducted a bibliometric analysis of AI research in sports injury prediction and prevention, together with its performance-related applications. Bibliographic records were retrieved from Scopus on 11 July 2026, with no restrictions on the publication year. After screening, 809 documents (694 articles and 115 reviews) published between 1997 and 2027 were analyzed using the Bibliometrix R-package and VOSviewer. Scientific production grew markedly from 2018 onward, increasing from 13 publications in 2018 to 204 by 2025. The corpus was distributed across 371 sources and 3,226 authors and accumulated 13,295 citations. China and the United States were the leading contributors, with closely comparable affiliation-based output. Keyword co-occurrence analysis produced a network of 44 keywords in 6 clusters, in which machine learning and artificial intelligence were the most central terms, closely linked to injury prevention, injury prediction, biomechanics, and wearable sensing. Thematic mapping identified injury prevention, injury risk, and wearable technology as well-developed central themes, while thematic evolution across three periods (1997–2018, 2019–2022, and 2023–2025) indicated a progression from early injury- and sports-specific research through methodological diversification toward applied sports analytics and athlete monitoring. These findings characterize the structure and trajectory of the published literature rather than the demonstrated effectiveness of AI tools in applied sports settings.

items.title: A closed loop multimodal auditing framework for enhancing artificial intelligence reliability in medical emergency response
items.abstract: Ensuring the reliability of AI-powered information retrieval systems is critical in high-stakes domains such as first aid. Traditional audit methodologies are often static, manual, and unimodal, failing to address the dynamic, time-sensitive, and multimodal requirements of these applications. To overcome these limitations, we introduce RADAR-FirstAid (Reliability-Aware Dynamic Auditing Framework), a closed-loop auditing pipeline — not a competing information system — for real-time, multimodal, and edge-aware auditing. Its key components include a Dynamic Query Simulator for generating criticality-weighted scenarios, a Multimodal Audit & Fusion Agent for verifying cross-modal consistency, a Differentiable Reliability Evaluator that employs LLM-based judges for automated assessment, and an Edge-Optimization Scheduler for efficient deployment. Applying the framework to a curated dataset of 1, 508 first-aid queries, we conduct a large-scale audit of Google’s AI Overviews (AIO) and Featured Snippets (FS), operated purely as black-box Systems under Audit. The audit reveals substantial reliability gaps: automated consistency scores of $$\Phi _{cons}=0.68$$ (FS) and 0.72 (AIO), safety/relevance scores of $$\Phi _{safe}=0.71$$ (FS) and 0.76 (AIO), and pronounced weaknesses on safety-critical “Binary” and “How-to” queries and on negative-sentiment queries where cautious tone matters most. Manual annotation on a 200-query subset validates the automated evaluation (Spearman $$\rho = 0.74$$ –0.87). Ablation studies confirm the essential role of each pipeline module, and geographical variance is minimal (SD $$<0.03$$ ). RADAR-FirstAid offers a scalable, automated, and reproducible audit instrument for AI-powered search systems in safety-critical domains.

items.title: A comprehensive review of advanced manufacturing techniques, ai-enabled design, and mechanical characterization of nature-inspired helicoidal hybrid composites for impact-resistant applications
items.abstract: Abstract Helicoidal structures mimic nature and are evident in plant cell walls, lamellar bone, and the shell structures of mantis shrimp and beetles. These nature-inspired helicoidal composites are widely used in impact-resistant applications. Traditional hand-layup methods for producing layered helicoidal composites can introduce defects such as gaps, overlaps, and wrinkles, which can be mitigated using Automated Fiber Placement (AFP). Optimizing AFP process parameters, including pressure, temperature, and layup speed, is crucial. While experimental optimization is costly and time-consuming, Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based design offers a more efficient alternative. This narrative review explores the inspiration behind helicoidal structures and their application fields. It also covers advanced manufacturing of hybrid long-fiber layered composites using AFP + autoclave/hot press, ceramic filler-based nanocomposites using direct ink writing (DIW), and multi-walled carbon nanotube (MWCNT)-based nanocomposites using digital micromirror device (DMD). Furthermore, it discusses the roles of machine learning and deep learning, coupled with finite element modeling, in minimizing process-induced defects. Compared with conventional AFP inspection techniques such as laser profilometry and thermography, a defect-detection algorithm based on PointNet + + , a convolutional neural network (CNN), can be tailored for 3D point cloud segmentation, offering a cost-effective, user-friendly alternative. Next, the mechanical and microstructural properties of helicoidal composites, compared with those of traditional laminates, are discussed to evalaute impact performance. Helicoidal composites with low inter-ply angles up to 20° consistently outperform conventional lay-ups under quasi-static and impact loading, due to a crack-twisting mechanism and superior out-of-plane properties. Incorporating nylon 6 powder microparticles into carbon/epoxy and glass/epoxy helicoidal composites subjected to impact loading significantly improves their toughness through self-healing, compared with virgin helicoidal composites. Carbon/epoxy helicoidal composites with low inter-ply angles of up to 9° are prone to extensive matrix cracking and minor fiber damage, while self-healing in carbon/epoxy composites also helps minimize matrix cracking but does not reduce fiber damage. In contrast, self-healing significantly decreases overall damage in glass/epoxy composites. Self-healing is more effective at eliminating damage in glass/epoxy than in carbon/epoxy, primarily because the former exhibits higher ductility (% elongation) than the latter.

items.title: A comprehensive study of skin lesion segmentation and classification using deep learning techniques
items.abstract: Deep learning has become an important computational approach in dermatology because it enables automated segmentation and classification of skin lesions. Manual dermoscopic analysis is time-consuming and depends on specialist expertise, with potential inter-observer variability. There is a need to develop reliable computer-aided diagnostic tools. This structured narrative review covers journal papers published mainly from 2018 to 2026 on skin lesion analysis with focus on image preprocessing, benchmark datasets, conventional machine learning approaches, convolutional neural networks, U-Net architectures, transfer learning approaches, Vision Transformers, attention-based models, ensemble solutions, and hybrid segmentation–classification systems. Building on present reviews covering individual tasks as well as broader segmentation–classification pipelines, the present work provides a critical development-to-deployment analysis connecting dataset characteristics, preprocessing, segmentation, classification, evaluation, explainability, robustness, fairness, computational requirements, and clinical applicability. The paper describes widely used evaluation metrics and explains why results obtained across different datasets, partitions, and experimental setups should not be directly compared. Major open problems include class imbalance, data bias, domain shift, limited representation of diverse skin tones, inadequate external validation, computational requirements, and limited explainability of efficient models. Emerging trends such as self-supervised learning, Transformers, foundation models, explainable AI, federated learning, and multi-modal clinical data are reviewed as well. The review offers practical advice to researchers and clinicians on how to approach the preprocessing, segmentation, classification, and evaluation of skin lesions and highlights priorities in developing clinically reliable skin lesion analysis systems.

items.title: A Comprehensive Survey on Misconception Diagnosis in AI-Assisted Programming Education: Rule-Based and LLM-Based Techniques, Accuracy-Cost Tradeoffs, and Open Challenges
items.abstract: A longstanding goal of programming-education tooling is to do more than mark an answer wrong and identify the specific misconception the novice programmer might have in their program. Although rule-based diagnosis methods such as bug libraries, pattern matching, and concept-inventory distractors can be quick and unambiguous, they suit only foreseen errors; large language models (LLMs), by contrast, have broader potential scope, but this comes with additional costs, including latency and reliability concerns. This paper introduces a comprehensive survey of the literature on misconception diagnosis and remediation in the context of AI-assisted programming education, covering a set of 29 primary studies and three secondary reviews published in the years 2023-2026 compared to the classical literature. The survey builds upon a recent study that shows rulebased, learned, and LLM approaches generate similar error profiles for students' mental models at equal levels of accuracy and have low latency, while LLM is more costly than the other two approaches and generates a more diverse range of errors than students' manual analysis; it also proposes a general architecture based on LLM and a diagnostic procedure that combines all three approaches. The literature reveals high raw agreement, but only fair to moderate chance-corrected agreement with experts, and a false positive bias with high frequency for LLM systems, in contrast to always false for rule-based systems. Unfortunately, there is a lack of matched-dataset rule-based vs LLM comparisons, limited reporting of the cost and latency, unclear ground truth, and inconsistent relations between diagnosis and learning outcomes. Directions for further research are given. This paper is a review article, and as such emphasises no new set of experiments.

items.title: A Conceptual Framework for Robust Explainable Deep Learning under Distribution Shifts and Noisy Data
items.abstract: Deep learning systems may experience performance degradation when deployed under distribution shifts, noisy data, and changing operational conditions. Furthermore, explanations generated by explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) methods may become unstable or unreliable under such conditions, limiting the interpretability and trustworthiness of model predictions. This paper proposes a conceptual Robust Explainable Deep Learning (R-XDL) framework that integrates data-quality assessment, distribution-shift and noise diagnostics, robust prediction, uncertainty estimation, explanation fidelity and stability assessment, risk-aware decision-making, human oversight, and controlled model adaptation. A conceptual mathematical objective and a risk-scoring mechanism are introduced to organise predictive robustness and explanation reliability within a unified lifecycle. The framework also proposes an explanation diagnostic gate that uses fidelity, stability, predictive uncertainty, and distribution-shift indicators to support decisions to accept a prediction, request human review, or defer automated decision-making. In addition, a proposed empirical evaluation protocol outlines the use of benchmark datasets, controlled corruption scenarios, appropriate baseline methods, calibration measures, explanation metrics, computational-cost analysis, and ablation studies. This manuscript presents a conceptual framework and proposed evaluation methodology; no experiments have been conducted, and no empirical performance results are claimed. Future research will implement and evaluate the framework to determine its effectiveness, limitations, and practical applicability. The proposed work provides a structured foundation for investigating the joint reliability of deep learning predictions and explanations under distribution shifts and noisy data.

items.title: A cross-sectional comparison of five large language models in answering Chinese-language patient queries on visual field defects associated with brain diseases
items.abstract: Background Visual field defects associated with brain diseases may arise from stroke, intracranial space-occupying lesions, and other central visual pathway disorders. Patient questions often span symptom recognition, explanation of causes, care triage, treatment, and rehabilitation. Large language models may improve access to patient education. However, their accuracy, logic, coherence, safety, and content accessibility have not been compared under controlled conditions in this high-risk, interdisciplinary Chinese-language setting. This study aimed to compare the performance of five selected large language models across multiple dimensions. Methods In this cross-sectional study, 30 fixed Chinese-language questions, refined by experts and phrased from a patient perspective, were submitted to ChatGPT 5.6 Sol, DeepSeek V4 Flash, Gemini 3.7 Flash, Qwen 3.8 Max, and Kimi K3 through a unified application programming interface (API) client. Each model generated one response per question in an independent single-turn session, with web retrieval disabled and conversation history cleared. Three raters, blinded to model identity, independently scored 150 randomly presented responses from 1 to 5 for accuracy, logic, coherence, safety, and content accessibility. Response time, word count, non-space character count, sentence count, paragraph count, and table count were also recorded. Models were compared using the Friedman test followed by Bonferroni-adjusted Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. Inter-rater agreement was assessed using Kendall’s W. Correlations were assessed using Spearman analysis with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction. Results Agreement among the three raters was high across all five dimensions (Kendall’s W = 0.820–0.844; all P < 0.001). The five models differed in accuracy, coherence, and content accessibility (P < 0.001, P < 0.001, and P = 0.001, respectively). No statistically significant between-model differences were observed in logic or safety (P = 0.247 and P = 0.061, respectively). ChatGPT 5.6 Sol had the highest median accuracy score [4.67 (interquartile range, 4.00–5.00)], and Kimi K3 had the highest median coherence score [4.50 (4.00–5.00)]. Both models had a median content accessibility score of 4.67 (4.00–5.00). Response time, response length, and text structure also differed among models. However, their correlations with expert quality scores were generally weak (|ρ| ≤ 0.279). Conclusion The five large language models exhibited distinctly multidimensional performance when answering Chinese-language patient questions about visual field defects associated with brain diseases. No single model consistently performed best across all clinically relevant dimensions. These findings are specific to the model versions tested on 15 August 2026; stability across repeated generations was not assessed. Response speed, length, and structure cannot substitute for direct assessment of medical quality. The absence of a statistically significant difference in safety ratings under controlled conditions does not imply equivalent or adequate clinical safety. Large language models are better suited to supporting patient education and clinician-patient communication under clinical supervision than to making diagnostic or treatment decisions independently.

items.title: A Deterministic Security Runtime for LLM Agents on MPI and Batch-Scheduled HPC Systems: Consensus-Governed, Hardware-Rooted Supervision of Every Rank
items.abstract: Large language model agents launch simulations on high-performance computing (HPC) systems, where one sbatch or mpirun can commit thousands of node-hours and a forged result can cost lives. Of 23 surveyed systems, none supervises the running job, and none holds when the control host is compromised. We fix both. Enclawed, our deterministic security runtime for AI agents, has until now served a single user; this work makes it a distributed runtime for parallel HPC and agent swarms. The Enclaweder, our hardware root of trust, keeps a compromised host from becoming a catastrophe. A launch gate decides every launch by policy alone, refusing what it cannot parse. Once the job runs, a swarm chain grants short leases against signed heartbeats and evicts on evidence, and a supervisor around every rank pauses it when its lease lapses and kills it on tampering. Each node signs with its Enclaweder's key, so the host can forge none of it. Enclawed needs no administrator privileges and plugs into existing clusters unchanged, over Secure Shell alone. Supervision leaves the compute loop of a 16-rank LAMMPS job unchanged, on graphics processors too, and adds about 3 s of start-up. Twelve live attacks on Enclaweder-keyed ranks, colluding coordinators included, ended fail-closed. Sixteen agents on a real model attempted 24 launches that planted instructions ordered; the gate denied all 24 and allowed all 108 legitimate ones. Enclawed's core and the HPC Agent Security Benchmark are open source.

items.title: A DIGITAL HUMANITIES APPROACH: PRACTICAL INSIGHTS INTO TRANSLATION STUDIES IN THE AI ERA
items.abstract: Translation Studies in the AI era are undergoing a profound transformation, yet a significant pedagogical gap persists: the disconnect between rapid computational advancement and the availability of accessible, reproducible training methodologies for instructors. The integration of AI, machine learning, and digital tools has reshaped traditional paradigms, prompting scholars to rethink the boundaries of translation studies today. This article addresses this challenge by establishing an integrative framework for "Applied Digital Humanities" within translation pedagogy. We propose and document two open-source computational solutions: a Python-based audio processor for MP3 segmentation and a customized "Consecutive Translation Trainer" designed to automate material preparation and enable the creation of CEFR-aligned, differentiated training corpora. The practical report suggests that Digital Humanities emerges as a powerful framework that bridges computational methods with humanistic inquiry. The integration of artificial intelligence into digital humanities has profoundly transformed the field of tra nslation studies, where the practical applications of AI technologies such as automated MP3 splitting, text-to-speech systems, AI assistants for code verification, and corpus-based approaches are highly valued. These technologies contribute to more efficient workflows, enhance linguistic research, and expand the methodological toolkit available to translation scholars.

items.title: A drone-assisted deep learning framework for disaster assessment in real time and emergency response
items.abstract: Disasters affect citizen safety, municipal infrastructure, and the economy, making disaster management vital and difficult. Rapid urban expansion and climatic extremes have increased big catastrophe frequency and complexity. Situational awareness and quick decision-making are needed. In catastrophes, traditional evaluation methods may not give accurate and timely information owing to enormous volumes of data and quick changes. Due to these restrictions, this research offers an AI system for real-time catastrophe assessment and response using drones and the Adaptive Convolutional-Transformer Fusion Network. Convolutional feature extraction and attention-based temporal modeling allow ACTF-Net to grasp sequential interactions and dynamic spatial patterns in high-dimensional catastrophic data. Adaptive Relevance Filtering and Contextual Scaling Transformation increase data dependability and feature relevance, enabling noisy or missing data learning. Testing regularly shows that ACTF-Net outperforms previous systems like BERT and CapsNet. F1-score is 0.981, area under curve is 0.993, and catastrophe severity prediction rate is 0.96. The model’s consistent performance across datasets of different sizes across time supports real-time applications. The proposed method uses multimodal drone data, powerful preprocessing, and novel metrics like the Contextual Sensitivity Index and Temporal Stability Score to reliably categorize and assess catastrophe severity using multiple labels. The results indicate that ACTF-Net may improve situational awareness, resource usage, and response time in high-risk crisis situations.
